TC1.Test Description: Validates I2C register default values and masked read/write behavior across the register map.
TC1.Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Check default values for all readable registers and record any mismatches.
2) For each of six data patterns, write to all writable registers not in the skip list.
3) Read back each register and compare against the masked expected value.
4) Report the result based on cumulative mismatch counters.
TC1.Impacted Registers: DEV_CTRL; TSFR_CTRL; SLV_ADDR; TGT_SLV_ADDR; I2C_MSTR_CODE; I2C_BYTE_CNT; SF_HCNT; SF_LCNT; I2C_HS_HCNT; I2C_HS_LCNT; RIS; MASK_INTR; INTR_STS; INTR_CLR; TAS; TX_FIFO_THLD; RX_FIFO_THLD; DMA_CTRL; FF; TX_FIFO_LVL; RX_FIFO_LVL; I2C_MSTR_STS; I2C_FLTR_SEL; I2C_CURRENT_BYTECNT; I2C_SMB_SFTRST; SMB_HST_STS; SMB_HST_CTRL; SMB_HST_CMD; SMB_HST_DATA0; SMB_HST_DATA1; SMB_HST_BLOCK_DATA; SMB_PEC_DATA; SMB_SLAVE_WDATA; SMB_SLAVE_CMD; SMB_SLAVE_CTS; SMB_SLV; SMB_NOTIFY_ADDR; SMB_NOTIFY_LOW_BYTE; SMB_NOTIFY_HIGH_BYTE; SMB_DATA_HLDTIME; SMB_TIMEOUT_CNT; SMB_TMEXT_CNT; I2CSMB_DATA_SETUP
TC1.Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- Default values match the expected reset values for all readable registers; any mismatch fails the test.
- For each data pattern, readbacks equal the computed masked expected value; any mismatch fails the test.
- The test passes if both default and read/write mismatch counters are zero.
TC1.Hidden_Test_Description: Test checks default reset values for all readable I2C registers and verifies masked write/read behavior using multiple data patterns. It uses arrays of addresses, default values, read/write masks, and a skip list.
TC1.Hidden_Remarks: Uses arrays: addr_array, default_value_array, read_mask_array, write_mask_array, skip_array. DEBUG_DISPLAY toggles additional prints. soft_reset_chk() present but not executed.
TC1.Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure:
Entry: test_case()
1. Call chk_rst_val().
   1.1 Loop entry: for i = 0 to CNT-1 (CNT = 43)
       - addr = addr_array[i]
       - If read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000: print skip message (if DEBUG_DISPLAY) and continue (no read)
       - READ: data_rd = read_reg(addr_array[i])
       - Compare: if (data_rd == default_value_array[i]) then PASS (optional print), else def_fail_cnt++ and print failure
   1.2 Loop exit condition: i == CNT
2. Call chk_rd_wr().
   2.1 Initialize chk_val[6] = {0xffffffff,0xaaaaaaaa,0x55555555,0x00000000,0xA5A5A5A5,0xffff0000}
   2.2 Outer loop entry: for j = 0..5
       - data_wr = chk_val[j]
       - Inner write loop entry: for i = 0..CNT-1
         * addr = addr_array[i]
         * If skip_array[i] == 1: (optional print) continue
         * If write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000: (optional print) continue
         * WRITE: write_reg(addr_array[i], data_wr)
       - Inner write loop exit condition: i == CNT
       - Inner readback loop entry: for i = 0..CNT-1
         * addr = addr_array[i]
         * If skip_array[i] == 1: (optional print) continue
         * If write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000: (optional print) continue
         * If read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000: (optional print) continue
         * READ: data_rd = read_reg(addr_array[i])
         * Compute: wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff)
         * Compute expected: exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i]))
         * Compare: if (data_rd == exp_val) PASS (optional print), else wr_fail_cnt++ and print failure
       - Inner readback loop exit condition: i == CNT
   2.3 Outer loop exit condition: j == 6
3. Termination: if (def_fail_cnt > 0 || wr_fail_cnt > 0) finish(1) else finish(0)
Timing: No waits in executed path. No ISRs. No DMA.
Register accesses (via addr_array macros):
- READ: read_reg(MIZAR_I2C_DEV_CTRL ... MIZAR_I2C_I2CSMB_DATA_SETUP) where readable per read_mask_array
- WRITE: write_reg(MIZAR_I2C_DEV_CTRL ... MIZAR_I2C_I2CSMB_DATA_SETUP) where writable per write_mask_array
Masks and conditions explicitly used per arrays.

TC2.Test Description: Transfers a data block from memory to I2C0 and then to I2C1 using DMA, verifies interrupt handling, and checks data integrity at the destination memory.
TC2.Remarks: Configures LSS NIC as non-secure slave interface via direct system register writes. Uses IRQ lines 80 and 81.
TC2.Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Configure system interrupt enable to allow I2C0 and I2C1 interrupts.
2) Initialize I2C0 and I2C1 control, interrupt, addressing, counters, FIFO thresholds, and DMA settings.
3) Preload the source SRAM buffer with five words.
4) Configure DMA channel 0 to move five words from the source SRAM buffer into the transmit block data register.
5) Wait until DMA activity clears.
6) Start the I2C0 transfer and poll the current byte count until zero.
7) Wait for the transfer complete interrupt and clear it through the system.
8) Enable I2C1 DMA and configure DMA channel 1 to move five words from the receive block data register to the destination SRAM buffer.
9) Wait until DMA activity clears.
10) Compare the five words in the source and destination buffers; all must match.
11) Report pass if no mismatches and the interrupt was properly cleared.

TC2.Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- The transfer complete interrupt occurs, is acknowledged, and both the controller and system interrupt status become cleared; otherwise the test fails.
- Each word in the destination buffer equals the corresponding word in the source buffer; any mismatch fails the test.
- The test passes when no errors are recorded at completion.

TC3.Test Description: Transfers a data block between two I2C instances using DMA in standard mode, handles the transfer complete interrupt, and verifies data integrity in memory.
TC3.Remarks: Configures LSS NIC as non-secure slave interface via direct register writes. Uses IRQ lines 80 and 81.
TC3.Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable system interrupts for the I2C controllers.
2) Initialize I2C0 and I2C1 control, clear pending interrupts, program addresses, byte counts, and standard-mode counters.
3) Set FIFO thresholds and enable DMA for transmission.
4) Preload the source SRAM buffer with five words.
5) Configure DMA channel 0 to move five words from the source SRAM buffer into the transmit block data register.
6) Wait until DMA channel enable clears.
7) Start the I2C0 transfer and poll the current byte count to zero.
8) Wait for the transfer complete interrupt and clear it through the system.
9) Enable I2C1 DMA and configure DMA channel 1 to move five words from the receive block data register to the destination SRAM buffer.
10) Wait until DMA channel enable clears.
11) Compare the five words in the source and destination buffers; all must match.
12) Report pass on zero errors.

TC3.Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- The transfer complete interrupt occurs and is cleared in both the controller and system; otherwise the test fails.
- Each word in the destination SRAM buffer equals the corresponding word in the source buffer; any mismatch fails the test.
- The test passes when no errors are recorded.
